caption:
A cup of flour isn't a measurement. It's a guess with a lid on it.

Scoop the cup and pack it, or spoon the flour in loose — the amount that lands in the bowl shifts either way, which is why two people can follow the same recipe and pull two different loaves out of the oven. Weight settles the argument: 120 grams is 120 grams no matter how it got there. The same scale also portions coffee, splits dough into equal pieces, and confirms a package's weight before a trip to the post office.

The Etekcity Food Kitchen Scale is a compact digital scale that reads exactly what's placed on it, so a recipe stops being an estimate. It carries 176,516 reviews at a 4.6-star average — a sample large enough that the score reflects how it performs across kitchens, not just one.

Recipes you already make turn out the same way twice, without changing anything else about how you cook. It's $10.99.
